vsa.narrative: Context now: downtrend (falling 50-day, above the 50-day, lower highs and lower lows); a test 23 Jul on volume 36% below average - a low-volume test inside the range (moderate significance); stopping volume 5 Aug on 4.7x volume, closed in the upper half - in an uptrend with buying behind it: bullish, at support / new lows (high significance); selling climax 6 Aug on 2.4x volume, closed on the low - climactic selling at the range lows: supply being absorbed, at support / new lows (high significance); two no-demand bars 14 Aug–24 Aug on volume 43% below average - but no demand, but strength has appeared in the background (low significance); a test 11 Sep on volume 29% below average - a test after climactic strength: the background has changed (moderate significance); upthrust 6 Oct on 0.9x volume, closed on the low - an upthrust in a downtrend - the highest-probability weakness, at resistance / new highs (high significance); last 5 bars: up bars on heavier volume (1.3x vs 0.7x) = demand in control; latest: no supply 7 Oct on 0.5x volume, closed off the lows - but in a downtrend a quiet down bar alone rarely turns it (low significance); balance neutral 41/100.

vsa_seq.lens: Williams lens (a tribute to Tom Williams's method): Background first: MDLN is in a downtrend, the VSA balance reads neutral (41/100), last key bar NS on 7 Oct. Holmes strength sequence S10 (reversal over two bars → no supply → no supply) completed 30 Sep: reversal over two bars 16 Sep → no supply 23 Sep → no supply 30 Sep. It confirms on a trade above 35.79; a close below 31.46 proves it wrong (triggered). Desk backtest for S10: edge (+0.11R over 1613 trades). Holmes strength sequence S9 (potential selling climax → no supply / test → demand overcoming supply) completed 29 Sep: potential climactic action / selling climax 18 Sep → no supply / test 23 Sep → demand overcoming supply 29 Sep. It confirms on a trade above 35.23; a close below 31.46 proves it wrong (triggered). Desk backtest for S9: noise (+0.02R over 734 trades).

biz.name: Medline Inc.
biz.desc: Medline Inc. manufactures med-surg products serving the hospital, surgery centers, physician offices, post-acute facilities, and nursing home sites of care in the United States and Internationally. It operates through two segments: Medline Brand and Supply Chain Solutions. The Medline Brand segment procures and manufactures products from three product categories include surgical solutions, front line care, and laboratory and diagnostics. Its front line care offers med-surg products for patient-facing needs, including wound care products, exam gloves, skin care and incontinence products, environment cleaning supplies, textiles, hand sanitizer, durable medical equipment, patient plastics, and decolonization and infection control products. Its surgical solutions provide operating room and perioperative environment product solutions, including surgical procedure trays, drapes and gowns, personal protective equipment, sterile wraps, surgical instruments, surgeon's gloves, procedure kits, and orthopedic implants. Its laboratory and diagnostics offer laboratory and diagnostic product solutions, including point of care testing, analyzers and instrumentation, lab and diagnostic consumables, diagnostic instruments, vital signs monitors, and anatomic pathology and phlebotomy products. It provides its products to domestic and international consumers. The Supply Chain Solutions segment procures and distributes a variety of third-party products from national brands. It provides logistics and supply chain optimization services to domestic and international consumers. It also provides supply chain optimization services, such as consulting engagements, outsourced warehouse and technology management, put-away-ready packaging, third-party logistics, inventory rationalization, and route planning. The company was founded in 1966 and is based in Northfield, Illinois.
